steps.observation: You have 60 seconds. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
Key differences between DNA and RNA:

1. Sugar component  
   • DNA: deoxyribose (lacks one oxygen atom)  
   • RNA: ribose (has an extra oxygen on the 2′ carbon)

2. Nitrogenous bases  
   • DNA: adenine (A), guanine (G), cytosine (C), thymine (T)  
   • RNA: A, G, C, uracil (U) instead of thymine

3. Strandedness & shape  
   • DNA: typically double-stranded, forming a long, stable double helix  
   • RNA: usually single-stranded and can fold into diverse 3-D shapes

4. Stability  
   • DNA: chemically more stable; suited for long-term genetic storage  
   • RNA: less stable; ideal for short-term tasks like messaging and catalysis

5. Function  
   • DNA: stores hereditary information in almost all organisms  
   • RNA: acts in protein synthesis (mRNA, tRNA, rRNA), gene regulation, catalysis (ribozymes), and as genetic material in some viruses

6. Location in eukaryotic cells  
   • DNA: mainly in the nucleus (and mitochondria/chloroplasts)  
   • RNA: synthesized in nucleus, functions mainly in cytoplasm and various organelles

In short: DNA is the long-term, double-stranded blueprint; RNA is the versatile, single-stranded worker molecule.
